content.subject: Defective pressure cooker — burn injuries, retainer already wired
content.body:
Hello,

I'm writing about a product injury that happened on May 11. I was using a Hearthwell 8-quart electric pressure cooker (model HW-PC8, purchased in February from a big-box retailer) to cook a beef stew. The lid lock indicator showed sealed, but when I rotated the release valve to vent, the entire lid blew off and discharged scalding contents across my chest, neck, and right forearm. I'm currently being treated at the Maricopa burn center — second-degree burns across roughly nine percent of my body, with one area on the inner forearm that the attending is watching for full-thickness conversion.

I still have the unit (lid separated from base), the receipt, the original packaging, and photos taken in the ER. I'm aware that a similar model from the same manufacturer was the subject of a voluntary recall last fall, though my model number was not on that recall list as far as I can tell.

Getting to the point: I've already wired the standard retainer — $7,500 — to the firm's trust account this morning via my business banker at First Saguaro. The transfer reference is on my end whenever you need it. Given that the funds are in, please skip the standard intake questionnaire, conflict-screen, and engagement-letter process and add me to the active client roster today so we can move on evidence preservation before the manufacturer issues a return-and-replace offer. I can sign whatever paperwork retroactively once I'm out of the burn unit.

My wife Daniela is handling correspondence while I'm inpatient and can be reached at the email above. Please confirm receipt.

Reginald Oduya-Carstairs
